item.title: Spark Program | ckb-msig: check and merge CKB multisig signatures from ckb-cli, Neuron and CCC (1 posts)
item.description: In our own words At ILE Labs we build tools. One of them, still under construction and private, led us to this gap: several parties putting together and signing one transaction. When we looked at how CKB’s own multisig payouts and contract upgrades get signed today, we saw the same manual step: signatures pasted into PR comments or chat, checked by eye, then trimmed by hand to exactly the threshold before ckb-cli will send. Fiber’s v0.7.0 upgrade has had enough signatures since 2 November and still isn’t on chain. We had to find out whether the wallets’ formats could be reconciled, so we built a prototype: ckb-msig 0.0.1 checks all six real signatures on that upgrade offline, with no keys...

item.title: Noir-CKB: the private tally is live on CKB testnet, try it yourself (2 posts)
item.description: Thanks for reading it this closely, and for the ideas. Voting is actually something I’ve spent a lot of time on. Earlier this year I built a ZK voting system for the Buidl Guidl challenge, and I wrote up everything that broke along the way: Anonymous Blockchain Voting is Impossible (I Was Wrong) The main thing I took from that was that the proof on its own doesn’t give you private voting. You need a commitment tree so people can prove they’re registered without saying which registration is theirs, a nullifier per election so nobody votes twice and you can’t follow the same voter across elections, and something like a paymaster, because the moment the voter’s own account pays the fee,...

item.title: Twine: Buy and Sell CKB Without Depositing on an Exchange (Fiber P2P PoC) (1 posts)
item.description: Thanks for going through the code carefully @ArthurZhang. Every point you raised was real. Here is what changed since 514c33a through 79788a8 (both directly from your notes and a few fixes around them): 1. Same hash algorithm on both legs Removed the hardcoded SHA-256 constant. Invoice parsing now reads hash_algorithm from /data/attrs, defaults to ckb_hash when omitted (matching Fiber v0.9.1), and rejects unknown or conflicting values. Before creating a hold, the daemon rejects unsupported algorithms on the buyer’s invoice, passes that invoice’s hash_algorithm to new_invoice for the hold, and verifies the created hold invoice matches it. item.title: React Native hooks for Fiber Network payments (`@fiber-pay/react-native`) (1 posts)
item.description: Hi everyone! I’ve been working on @fiber-pay/react-native for my CKBuilders capstone and wanted to share where it stands. The idea came from looking at khie-mobile, a React Native wallet for CKB. It doesn’t support Fiber payments yet. fiber-pay already has React hooks, but those run a Fiber node in the browser through WASM and IndexedDB, so they don’t fit React Native. When I read through @fiber-pay/sdk, I found that its FiberRpcClient only needs fetch. That meant I could use the existing client and connect to a remote fnn node over JSON-RPC, instead of trying to run a node on the phone. The package has two hooks so far: useFiberNode({ url }) connects to the node and exposes its status...

item.title: QuotaCell: Let your team spend without handing over the treasury (1 posts)
item.description: Ticoworld: QuotaCell delegate key, without needing access to the owner’s key? Thanks @Ticoworld, and sorry for the slow follow-up. I wanted to check this properly against how CSR actually works before answering. The honest answer: yes, technically, but it doesn’t add much. A CSR job can’t carry a key of its own. Every CSR runner signs its transactions with its own service key, and services never see that key. So the only way to use a QuotaCell delegate today would be to register one specific runner’s key as the delegate. The owner’s key would never be needed, but the refill would then depend on that single runner being online. That’s essentially what Ayoub already has with his keeper bot,...
